:tutorial/content "Given a collection of $n$ objects, there are $n!$ ways to arrange those objects in a sequence.

- For example, suppose we have $n=2$ objects: $A$ and $B.$ Then there are $2!=2 \cdot 1 = 2$ arrangements:

$$
\underbrace{A,B}_{1\text{st way}}, \quad \underbrace{B,A}_{2\text{nd way}}
$$

- Likewise, suppose we have $n=3$ objects: $A,$ $B,$ and $C.$ Then there are $3!=3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 = 6$ arrangements:

$$
\underbrace{A,B,C}_{1\text{st way}},\quad
\underbrace{A,C,B}_{2\text{nd way}}, \quad 
\underbrace{B,A,C}_{3\text{rd way}}, \quad 
\underbrace{B,C,A}_{4\text{th way}}, \quad 
\underbrace{C,A,B}_{5\text{th way}},\quad 
\underbrace{C,B,A}_{6\text{th way}}
$$

This pattern extends to any number of objects." :tutorial/id #uuid "0753e8b5-a022-5644-84fc-f43f1dcf6761" :tutorial/math-academy-id 3680 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "c7acf227-0405-52eb-b5a9-6874c264b053" :step/math-academy-id 20565 :step/next {:db/id 17592186084114}} {:db/id 17592186084114 :step/content {:db/id 17592186083219 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186083019 :question/id #uuid "d39c9a9a-e44b-5673-b930-25576c8a54a3" :question/math-academy-id "e-5671"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "74677256-e307-5d49-b7e0-c3f4e79cf818" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049300} {:db/id 17592186049341}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186083602} {:db/id 17592186083844} {:db/id 17592186237956} {:db/id 17592186237957} {:db/id 17592186284784} {:db/id 17592186287966} {:db/id 17592186332929} {:db/id 17592186335791} {:db/id 17592186335799} {:db/id 17592186392656} {:db/id 17592186395905}] :knowledge-point/title "Calculating the Number of Ways That N Objects Can Be Arranged"} :step/id #uuid "55717602-2643-55f3-9ba3-f1359bfa5ed3" :step/math-academy-id 20566 :step/next {:db/id 17592186084115}} {:db/id 17592186084115 :step/content {:db/id 17592186084447 :tutorial/content "The mathematical name for an arrangement is a **permutation**. \underbrace{B,C,A}_{4\text{th way}}, \quad
